Tata Aig General Insurance Company office at:15th Floor, Tower A Karam Marg Lower Parek Mumbai ......Insurance Company/Respondent no.3 Date of accident : 06.11.2023 Result of accident : Simple injury Date of filing of Dar : 07.03.2024 Date of Decision : 16.12.2025 Mact no.453/2024 Seema vs. Vinay & ors. Page no. 1 of 20 ss Digitally signed by Charu Charu gupta gupta Date: 2025.12.16 16:56:36 +0530 Award 1. The present detailed accident report arises out of road accident in which one Seema aged about 40 years, suffered injuries. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 06.11.2023 upon receipt of PCR call vide DD no.11A, Ct. Mohit reached the spot i.e. Archana Red light, BRT road, Greater Kailash-I, where vehicle no.DL-12CR-7508 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) was found in accidental condition.
texts.facts: 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 06.11.2023 upon receipt of PCR call vide DD no.11A, Ct. Mohit reached the spot i.e. Archana Red light, BRT road, Greater Kailash-I, where vehicle no.DL-12CR-7508 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) was found in accidental condition. Victim Seema was informed to be sustained injuries. 3. An FIR No.291/23 was registered u/s 279/337/304A IPC was registered at PS Greater Kailash. Police investigated the matter. During investigation, it was revealed by one Harish that on 06.11.2023 while he was crossing BRT road alongwith 2-3 other women, at about 7 AM, a gray colour car bearing no.DL-12CR-7508 came from Moolchand side at a very high speed, driven in rash and negligent manner and hit Harish as well as those 2-3 other ladies. All the victims were rushed to AIIMS Trauma center in PCR. Victims Seema and Harish Salikram Soni sustained simple injuries while victims Rekha Devi and Neeru succumbed to the fatal injury. 4. During investigation, breath analyzer test was conducted on the driver of the offending vehicle wherein breath alcohol 290mg/100ml. was found. Page no. 2 of 20 ss Digitally signed by Charu Charu Date: gupta gupta 2025.12.16 16:56:39 +0530 section 5/180,3/180 & 185 of MV Act was filed against the driver and owner of the offending vehicle before concerned criminal court while four separate DARs were filed in respect of four victims before this Tribunal. 5. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3. 6. Despite opportunity, no reply or written statement was filed by Respondent no.1 and 2. In its reply filed by the insurance company, a statutory defence of breach of insurance policy has been taken. It has been pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle was under the influence of alcohol as his blood report reveals 290mg/100ml of alcohol for which Section 185 MV Act has also been invoked by the police. It is also pleaded that such driver of the offending vehicle was driving without a valid driving licence, for which Section 3/181 MV Act and Section 5/181 MV Act has been invoked by the police. It is thus pleaded that the insurance company is not liable to compensate the petitioners. 7. From the pleadings, following issues were framed on 20.01.2025. In order to prove his claim, petitioner examined hermself MACT no.453/2024 Seema vs. Vinay & ors. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. She deposed on the lines of the DAR claiming that on 06.11.2023 at about 7:30 a.m, she was going to Kailash Colony for her work. When she was crossing red light at BRT Road along with 2-3 other persons, a gray color car bearing n o.DL-12CR-7508, came at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit her. Due to this, victim fell on the road. An unknown person called PCR. Victim was removed to AIIMS Trauma Center where she was medically examined. PW-1 further deposed that she was working as a housemaid and earning of Rs.15,000/- per month. He relied upon her Adhar card as Ex.PW1/1 and complete DAR as Ex.PW1/2. He was duly cross examined by counsel for insurance company. Respondent no.3/insurance company also led its evidence by examining one Daksh Arora as R3W1/1 who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R3W1/A. He relied upon insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/1, notice issued u/O 12 Rule 8 CPC as Ex.R3W1/2, postal receipts as Ex.R3W1/3 and Ex.R3W1/4. He was duly cross examined by learned counsel for petitioner. As per discharge summary prepared at JPN Apex Trauma Center (AIIMS), injured was diagnosed with injuries including abrasion old healed injury, scab on left forearm on extensor aspect of around 4X3 cm. Total compensation after deduction Rs.16,000/- Interest: Simple interest @7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till actual realization of Award amount/ compensation. 21. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 7.5% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. 22. The total compensation payable to the claimant would be Rs.16,000/- with simple interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of DAR till its actual realization with by respondents.
texts.arguments: In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 13. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam Insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 18.6. It was observed by Apex Court in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability --Item (ii) (a). 17.7. However, in a recent judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India titled as Parminder Singh vs Honey Goyal on 18 March, 2025 in S.L.P. (C) No. 4484 OF 2020 has held that : "17. 29. In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation".
